📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A school in the UK has sent staff out in a minibus to bring absent pupils to class during GTA 6’s launch week, while also offering a prize draw to students who attend every day.

GTA 6 is finally here, and for many, the allure of taking a sick day to sneak in some extra game time is proving too strong. In fact, some workplaces, like this California-based car company, gave employees the day off to play.

In a recent development, an army unit in the United States even offered troops a four-day pass to play GTA 6 as part of their incentives to re-enlist, with 20 soldiers taking up the offer. Then there was a KFC in Australia that hosted a funeral for a fake person, just so customers have a valid reason to take the day off work.

However, a school in the UK is desperately trying to keep students in school by using a minibus to catch those who try to skip class in order to play Rockstar’s latest open-world outing.

According to ITV News, Ninestiles Academy in Birmingham has sent staff into the local community in a minibus to bring pupils to school during GTA 6’s launch week.

“We have been working hard to make this a particularly engaging and positive week for our learners, with a range of activities designed to encourage strong attendance,” noted principal Alex Hughes.

“This has included careers-focused assemblies and information events, colleagues visiting the local community in our school minibus to help bring learners into school and a prize draw for everyone who achieves 100% attendance across the week.”.

Ninestiles has not remarked whether any pupils brought in by minibus missed class because they were playing GTA 6, but its more direct approach to tackling convenient absences around GTA 6’s launch is just one of several ways schools have responded.

Another school in England offered students the chance to win an $85 Amazon voucher for attending on launch day, while a professor in Spain actually canceled homework and postponed an exam to give students more time to play.

Take-Two CEO is shutting down questions about GTA 7 just days after GTA 6’s launch

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Rockstar released GTA 6 on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait for a latest numbered Grand Theft Auto.
  • But while players are only just getting their first look at Vice City and the rest of Leonida, some are already looking ahead to the next entry in the series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick is already being asked about GTA 7, despite GTA 6 only being days old.

Rockstar released GTA 6 on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, ending a 13-year wait for a latest numbered Grand Theft Auto.

But while players are only just getting their first look at Vice City and the rest of Leonida, some are already looking ahead to the next entry in the series.

On launch day, Zelnick joined the TBPN podcast to talk about the release, and was asked early on about when GTA 7 could drop, to which he answered: “Once you get through several hundred hours of the most incredible fun you’ve ever heard, ask the question again.”.

Later in the interview, he was asked about the sequel again and how substantial the map could be, given that GTA 6 covers a huge city and a surrounding state.

“Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?” one of the hosts asked, with Zelnick clearly amused by the question.

“We at Take-Two just went live with GTA 6 on November 19,” he jokingly replied. “Let me check my watch. Oh, it’s still November 19. And you’re asking a question about GTA 7. I mean guys, really?”.

Recent findings suggest that jordi: "Theoretically, GTA 7 could just be a live version of the entire world, right?"@StraussZelnick, the CEO behind GTA 6: "We went live with GTA 6 on November 19. Let me check my watch. Oh, it's still November 19. And you're asking a question about GTA 7." pic.twitter.com/sHdVawdln2.

He then mentioned a quote his father used to say about past achievements being “yesterday’s headlines,” but then quipped: “It’s not even yesterday.”.

With GTA 6 only just arriving, it will likely be years before we get any concrete information about its potential follow-up. However, Zelnick has hinted that Rockstar’s future games won’t take as long to make.

Plus, we still have GTA 6 Online to look forward to, which should tide players over until GTA 7.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A brand-latest phone that doesn’t connect to the internet has been launched in Japan, and it looks like the classic Nokia phones that you might remember.

For years, smartphone people have been trying to find creative solutions to cut down their screen time, especially as phones have started doing weekly reviews of app usage and screen time.

Some have opted to set time limits on the apps they can use, while others have created heavyweight cases that will quite literally force you to work out in order to use your smartphone.

Recent findings suggest that in other cases, some people have taken a step back in time, ditching their smartphones for flip phones and devices that don’t actually connect to the internet. These throwback phones have popped up across Europe and the United States, and now Japan is getting in on the act with a upcoming device.

As per The Japan Times, Japan’s KDDI Corporation has introduced a mobile phone with “minimal functions.”.

Named the Infobar Zero, it will be available to pick up on Christmas Day, and is limited to calls, text messages, and other basic features. Owners won’t have the ability to connect to the internet, but it will have a camera and a music player.

While it isn’t a complete recreation of Nokia’s iconic 3310 phone, the Infobar Zero does strike up plenty of comparisons to that classic device.

Additionally, the ‘dumbphone’ isn’t aimed at replacing your smartphone, but rather providing a break from the smartphone life.

It has been planned by KDDI for quite some time, just as a way of relieving the reliance to live life on apps.

Owners will be able to register their phone numbers on the Zero and a smartphone as part of KDDI’s “two numbers” system – sort of like using an eSIM in some parts of the world.

Microsoft outage brings fax machines back into action across Japanese offices.

$499 flip phone that blocks all social media revealed by console maker Commodore.

This newly introduced phone is built to break your social media addiction.

You will be able to keep your smartphone at home when you go to school or work, and then return to using it later in the day, if that’s how you choose to live.

Elsewhere, a latest app called Island has been debuted, and the farming simulator-like game will actually punish you for spending too much time on it.

GTA 6 players report game-breaking crashes on PS5 and Xbox

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 players are reporting crashes on PS5 and Xbox, with some even unable to get past the opening minutes of the game.
  • While many GTA 6 fans across PlayStation and Xbox are enjoying their time in Leonida, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows for everyone trying to explore Rockstar’s latest installment.
  • Since its November 19 release, players have reported game-breaking crashes that prevent them from progressing through the main story and even playing altogether.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players are reporting crashes on PS5 and Xbox, with some even unable to get past the opening minutes of the game.

While many GTA 6 fans across PlayStation and Xbox are enjoying their time in Leonida, it’s not all sunshine and rainbows for everyone trying to explore Rockstar’s latest installment.

Since its November 19 release, players have reported game-breaking crashes that prevent them from progressing through the main story and even playing altogether.

In a Reddit post, one PS5 player remarked the game had worked flawlessly until they reached Pipework, one of the game’s early missions, where you are introduced to Mandy.

It has been revealed that “It crashes every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it,” they wrote, adding that they can no longer progress through the story. “You would think the plane flying was intensive, but it crashes every time I use the plunger or stand around the sink with it. I just paid $125 for my PS5 to be repaired and $100 for the game, this is ridiculous.”.

Others are running into problems much earlier, with a PS5 Pro owner revealing the game crashes as the opening prologue begins.

“Game keeps crashing at the exact same point during the opening prologue. I’m using a PS5 Pro and have been unable to play since launch. The game crashes immediately as the startup prologue begins, either at the exact same point or a couple of seconds into it, displaying error code CE-108255-1.”.

According to recent reports, when checking the PlayStation Support page, error CE-108255-1 prompts players to simply “try updating your game”. However, GTA 6 fans who have encountered this glitch on PS5 have reported that clearing the console’s cache, rebuilding its database, factory resetting the PS5, and downloading the game three times has done nothing to alleviate the problem.

In a recent development, “Despite all this, the problem persists. It crashes at the same point every single time,” they wrote. “I’m honestly extremely disappointed and frustrated at this point. I’ve exhausted almost every troubleshooting step available online and still haven’t been able to play.”.

According to recent reports, the reports are not limited to PlayStation, either, as some Xbox Series X players have also reported crashes within minutes of play. “The game sometimes even crashes after only 15 minutes. The first crash happened about 2 hours after I started playing, and ever since that it kept crashing,” added another player.

Rockstar’s GTA 6 troubleshooting page currently directs players experiencing console errors to PlayStation or Xbox support, but hopefully a patch will fix this matter sooner rather than later.

Animal control called to rescue alligator that turned out to be a pool floatie

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (391 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Animal control was forced to respond to a call about an alligator on the loose, but it turned out to be just a pool floatie.
  • Over the years, plenty of people have rushed to call emergency services to report something that, when investigated, turned out to be totally false.
  • According to recent reports, this was the case over in Sugar Land, Texas, on November 12 when animal control received a call about an alligator being on the loose.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Animal control was forced to respond to a call about an alligator on the loose, but it turned out to be just a pool floatie. Seriously.

Over the years, plenty of people have rushed to call emergency services to report something that, when investigated, turned out to be totally false.

According to recent reports, this was the case over in Sugar Land, Texas, on November 12 when animal control received a call about an alligator being on the loose. As per Sugar Land Animal Services, they were told that the gator appeared to be feeling a bit sick and in need of some assistance.

Sources indicate that yet, when they reached it, it wasn’t all it seemed. “When ASO Perez arrived on the scene to investigate, she was in for a significant surprise. What looked very real from a distance turned out to be a runaway pool floatie!” they posted on Facebook.

“While this call definitely gave our team a good laugh, we always take every report seriously,” Animal Services added.

Sources indicate that in the photo, the inflatable gator had its mouth stuck open with teeth on show, so if you see it from a distance, you might be confused. However, up close, you can tell it’s meant to be lounged on, not hunted or scared of.

It has been revealed that “Remember: if you ever spot wildlife that looks sick or injured, please keep a safe distance and call the experts to handle it. You never know if it’s the real deal!”.

Sources indicate that naturally, commenters saw the funny side of things too. “Well, that was a rather inflated story then,” one joked. “She is very brave! Thank you, Officer Perez, for all you do,” another added. “Wow. It looks so realistic! Crazy,” another replied.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chipotle is bringing back its Thanksgiving BOGO promotion, giving customers a chance to score a free meal ahead of the holiday.

The fast food chain announced on November 20 that its Back Home BOGO deal will return for one night only, allowing Rewards members to get two meals for the price of one at participating US restaurants.

Sources indicate that the promotion first debuted in 2025 and became Chipotle’s largest sales-driving campaign of the year. Its return comes as millions of Americans prepare to travel home and reconnect with friends and family over Thanksgiving weekend.

On Wednesday, November 25, Chipotle Rewards members can receive a free meal when purchasing another one of equal or greater value between 5 p.m. and 9 p.m. local time.

To redeem the offer, customers must visit a participating US Chipotle restaurant and scan their Rewards membership card at checkout.

The promotion is available exclusively in restaurants, meaning orders placed through the Chipotle app, website, delivery services, or third-party platforms will not qualify.

It has been revealed that customers can receive up to five free meals per check, provided they purchase an meal of equal or greater value for each free item. Kids’ meals do not count toward the promotion.

“Thanksgiving Eve is when the hometown group chat comes to life,” said Stephanie Perdue, Chipotle’s Senior Vice President of Brand Marketing.

Recent findings suggest that “Whether Chipotle is the first stop of the night or where the crew ends up later, we’re giving friends a place to get together over real food. The response last year revealed us how much our guests embraced the occasion, and we’re excited to bring it back as another reason for hometown crews to reconnect before Thanksgiving.”.

Chipotle is giving away free food to anyone with a tattoo for one hour only.

Chipotle is offering $6 entrees on Halloween to customers who wear costumes.

Chipotle releases School Spirit BOGO with free entrees for back-to-school season.

The company cited Morning Consult research showing that 76% of Gen Z consumers visit restaurants to socialize with friends and family, highlighting the role dining out plays in holiday gatherings.

Chipotle is also offering a separate promotion following Thanksgiving, giving customers a $0 delivery fee on qualifying orders from November 27 through November 30.

Sources indicate that to claim the delivery offer, customers must enter the code CYBER26 when ordering through Chipotle’s app or website. The deal requires a minimum purchase of $10 in the US or $12 in Canada, excluding taxes and fees.

Although the delivery fee will be waived, customers may still face higher menu prices and additional service fees.

Both promotions are available for a limited time at participating locations, with the Thanksgiving BOGO ending at 9 p.m. local time on November 25.

Bisht also claimed that she had received threatening messages from anonymous Instagram accounts discussing her movements and daily routine.

A man has been charged with felony retail theft after police say he posed as a Walmart delivery driver to steal Pokemon cards from a store in Dodgeville, Wisconsin.

Sources indicate that dodgeville police identified the man as Charles L. LaChapelle. According to WMTV 15 News, investigators allege he took merchandise from the store during pickups while posing as a Spark driver. Spark is Walmart’s app for independent drivers who pick up and deliver customer orders.

Recent findings suggest that the cards were from Pokemon’s 30th Celebration expansion, which launched on September 16 with 30 different foil Pikachu cards, one in each booster pack. The set arrived weeks after Walmart began holding online drawings for some Pokemon card releases.

Officers responded to a report of a theft in progress at the Dodgeville Walmart Supercenter shortly after 11:15 a.m. local time on November 19. They pulled over a black Tesla with Florida plates and mentioned a search turned up 125 packages of 30th Celebration boosters.

Police also recovered 112 packages of One Piece trading cards, 26 Pokemon anniversary tin sets, and a Rayquaza Lego set, along with other merchandise still in its packaging.

Sources indicate that police stated the Tesla had traveled to several locations in Wisconsin and Minnesota, as well as Missouri. The department is asking other agencies to come forward if they can link any of the additional merchandise to thefts in their area.

In a separate case in September, an Ohio collector was sentenced to 90 days of GPS monitoring after putting a tracker on a van used to deliver Pokemon cards to Walmart.

The developers of One-armed Robber are asking players to spend their surprise refunds in the free Steam heist game after a hacker sent the money back without the studio’s permission.

Duhndal released One-armed Robber in December 2023. The first-person game lets players rob banks and stores solo or with friends, with each robber limited to one arm. Crews can sneak into a vault or fight their way through, then haul out as much loot as they can carry. The game has roughly 54,000 Steam reviews, according to SteamDB.

On November 20, Duhndal stated someone gained access to one of its Steamworks API keys and used it to ban players and concern refunds for in-game purchases. The studio said the incident affected a small share of its player base.

Recent findings suggest that the refunds went to players who had never asked for their money back. Duhndal stated the transactions caused “significant financial losses” for its small team. The studio gave no figure for the losses or how many refunds were issued.

It has been revealed that duhndal asked players who want to help it recover to put some of their refund toward another purchase in One-armed Robber or one of the studio’s other games. It also announced a sale on heist maps for players looking to pick up missions they don’t already own.

“This is completely optional! You haven’t done anything wrong, and you don’t owe us anything,” the developer said.

Sources indicate that duhndal said it revoked the compromised key and lifted all unauthorized bans. Players who were unfairly banned should now be able to get back into the game.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

It has been revealed that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Getting shortlisted for a junior data analyst job depends less on how many courses you have finished and more on what you can show. This strategy breaks preparation into eight skill areas, pairs each one with a learning option and a hands-on task, and gives you a simple test for knowing when to move on.

It has been revealed that many people preparing for their first analyst role study for months and still struggle to get interviews. Their CVs list SQL, Excel and Tableau, yet nothing on the page demonstrates those tools being used to answer a real question. Recruiters reading dozens of similar applications need something more concrete.

According to recent reports, A course can give your learning a sensible order, but a completion badge indicates little about how you think. A small analysis that states its question, explains its method and admits its limits tells a hiring manager far more. This strategy aims to collect that kind of proof while you learn, not after.

In a recent development, start by collecting ten to twenty entry-level postings in the industry you want to join, and tally the tools and tasks they mention. You will quickly see a pattern. Some roles are built around Excel and routine reporting, while others want SQL, a BI platform and a bit of Python.

The wider market follows a similar shape. Jobright’s 2026 analysis of data analyst hiring, which looked at 2025–2026 postings from LinkedIn, Indeed and Levels.fyi, found that more than 80% of data analyst jobs mention SQL, over 60% mention Excel or Google Sheets, and roughly half mention Python or R. Let your own tally decide the order you learn in, but expect SQL to sit near the top.

As you work through each area below, finish with something you can show someone: a query, a tidied dataset, a chart, a one-page report or a portfolio project. Free material is often enough if you can stay disciplined. Pay for teaching only when it gives you something you cannot get alone, such as feedback, accountability or a fixed timetable.

SQL is how analysts pull, join and summarise records from a database, and a tool like Tableau lets other people explore what you found. Treat them as one workflow rather than two subjects: frame a question, write the query, sanity-check the numbers and present the result so a non-technical reader can follow it.

Industry observers note that SQLBolt offers free, bite-sized SQL lessons that run in the browser, and Tableau publishes free training videos on connecting to data and building dashboards. Used together, they are enough to produce a small end-to-end project.

If you learn better with a set schedule and an instructor checking your work, you could learn to analyse data with SQL and Tableau from scratch through a guided programme at Heicoders Academy in Singapore. Whichever route you take, compare what is covered, how feedback is given, when sessions run and the full cost against what free resources already offer.

Proof you can show: A working SQL query set and your first published dashboard.

Move on when: You can take a question from idea to dashboard on your own, without following a tutorial line by line.

In a recent development, spreadsheets are still where much of a team’s day-to-day reporting lives, especially when colleagues don’t write SQL. Get comfortable with filtering, pivot tables, and lookup functions, and learn to spot quiet errors like dates saved as text or one category spelled three different ways.

Sources indicate that the next step is automating the cleanup so it doesn’t have to be repeated by hand each month. Microsoft’s Power Query documentation highlights how to import and reshape data in recorded steps that refresh when newly introduced data arrives. The same ideas apply in other spreadsheet tools too.

Proof you can show: A messy export turned into a summary that refreshes itself.

Move on when: You can clean an untidy CSV and build a report that updates when the source file changes.

Sources indicate that for most junior analyst roles, the technical interview is a SQL test. Basic SELECT statements won’t be enough; interviewers like to probe joins, subqueries, common table expressions and window functions, which answer everyday questions such as running totals or each customer’s first purchase.

Practise with timed problem sets and review your answers for correctness as well as speed.

Proof you can show: Confidence going into a live or take-home SQL test.

Move on when: You can solve intermediate problems in around 15 to 20 minutes each without looking up syntax.

Sources indicate that take-home assignments often come with data that has been made messy on purpose. Reviewers want to see how you deal with missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats, and whether they can follow your reasoning afterwards.

Industry observers note that keep a short cleaning log as you work, noting each change and why you made it. A separate sheet tab or a list of comments in a notebook both work.

Proof you can show: A take-home submission a reviewer can audit step by step.

Move on when: Every change to your dataset is written down with a reason.

Sources indicate that case-study questions test whether you can read numbers sensibly, not just produce them. A working grasp of distributions, means and medians, spread, correlation and sampling will keep you away from the mistakes that undo otherwise good answers, such as quoting an average that a few extreme values have pulled out of shape.

Proof you can show: Clear, careful answers in case-study interviews.

Move on when: You can explain in everyday language why two things moving together doesn’t mean one causes the other.

Industry observers note that every chart should help someone answer a specific question. Learn where bars, lines, scatter plots and simple tables each work best, and how axis ranges, labels and colour can nudge a reader towards the wrong conclusion. On a dashboard, the most notable finding should be the first thing people see.

It has been revealed that datawrapper’s guidance on picking chart types is a useful free reference. As practice, show the same result in two different chart types and decide which one represents the data more honestly.

Proof you can show: Portfolio charts that make a point, not just show off features.

Move on when: A person who has never seen your data can spot the main finding and its caveat at a glance.

Industry observers note that what counts as a useful metric depends on the role. Marketing analysts focus on conversion and retention, operations analysts on delivery times and capacity, and finance analysts on margins and cash flow. Choose one sector and learn exactly how its key measures are defined.

Proof you can show: A project built around the questions your target industry actually asks.

Move on when: You can define several sector metrics and describe how a manager would use each one.

Your portfolio is where the other seven areas come together. Two or three deep, well-documented projects will say more about you than a long list of quick ones. Give each project a README that sets out the question, the data, your method, the findings and the limitations.

Proof you can show: A portfolio link and a write-up you can talk through in an interview.

Move on when: Every project clearly explains what it asked, how you answered it and what you found.

It has been revealed that there is no need to finish all eight areas before you apply. Once you can use the tools your target roles mention, speak honestly about your work and point to two or three clearly explained projects, start sending applications and keep learning alongside them.

Sources indicate that adjust each application to the job. Lead with a reporting example for spreadsheet-heavy roles, a query that solved a real problem for SQL roles, and a chart that supported a decision for visualisation roles. Be upfront about which work you built independently and which came from guided exercises.

Do I really need eight courses? No. These are skill areas, not eight required qualifications. A single resource can cover several of them, and practice you do on your own counts as much as classroom learning.

Sources indicate that is it possible to prepare using only free material? Yes. Free tutorials, open textbooks, official documentation and public datasets cover the fundamentals well. The harder parts are sticking to a routine and finding people who will give you honest feedback.

It has been revealed that which should come first, SQL or spreadsheets? It depends on the jobs you want. Spreadsheets are an easy starting point for reporting roles, while SQL is expected wherever databases are involved. You will want both eventually, so start with whichever your target postings stress most.

In a recent development, how many portfolio projects should I have? Two or three solid ones are a good start. Each should show a clear question, steps someone else could repeat and an honest reading of the results, rather than several near-identical dashboards.

It has been revealed that do I need a certificate before I apply? Not usually. Some employers ask for one, but many judge skills through interviews, take-home tasks and tests instead. Go by what each posting actually requires.

Taco Bell is turning up the heat with a newly introduced ‘Make It Flamin’ Hot’ customization option that lets customers add spicy Fritos to some of their favorite menu items.

The fast-food giant has confirmed a new limited-time feature that allows customers to upgrade eligible orders with Fritos Flamin’ Hot chips, adding an extra layer of spice and crunch.

Starting November 24, the customization will be available at participating locations through December 9, giving customers the chance to experiment with some fiery combinations.

According to Taco Bell’s official announcement, customers can add the chips to popular items including the Crunchwrap Supreme, Cantina Chicken Rolled Quesadilla, and the returning Naked Chicken Chalupa.

The announcement follows Taco Bell’s recent introduction of the Flamin’ Hot Grilled Cheese Burrito and Flamin’ Hot Mini Taco Salad, the latter of which was first revealed alongside more than 20 new products earlier in 2026.

“When Taco Bell fans love a menu item, they find ways to make it their own,” said Liz Matthews, Taco Bell’s Global Chief Food Innovation Officer.

“That creativity constantly inspires us, and Make It FLAMIN’ HOT is our way of putting some of that Test Kitchen magic directly into their hands.”.

Customers can access the newly introduced customization through Taco Bell’s mobile app, website, self-service kiosks, or by ordering at participating restaurants.

Simply select an eligible menu item, choose the “Customize” or “Modify” option, and add Fritos Flamin’ Hot from the available toppings.

However, there are some restrictions. Crunchy tacos, the Cheesy Gordita Crunch, a la carte Nacho Fries, beverages, and desserts are excluded from the promotion.

In a recent development, wanda Dench and Jamal Hinton first made headlines in 2016 when a mistaken text message led to the pair celebrating Thanksgiving together. What started as an accidental invitation has since become an annual tradition, with the two continuing to reunite for the holiday.

Now, their friendship is heading to television after the pair signed a deal with Lifetime to bring their story to the screen, with a movie expected to arrive in November 2027.

Dench confirmed to The Arizona Republic on November 16 that she and Hinton recently signed over the rights to their story for a Lifetime movie currently titled ‘The Thanksgiving Grandma.’.

The film is expected to begin production in early 2027, with producer Jack Leslie targeting a November release that same year.

“They did tell us right up front that it’s based on our story,” Dench explained.

Hinton also declared the news on Instagram, sharing a photo alongside Dench and celebrating their partnership with Lifetime.

Recent findings suggest that “Very excited to officially be in business with Lifetime!” he wrote. “They believe in our story, and it truly feels like we’re in the best hands as we take this next step.”.

He also thanked Dench for being a constant source of support throughout their friendship, telling followers that their journey was only getting started.

It has been revealed that the pair’s story began in November 2016 when Dench accidentally texted Hinton while attempting to invite her grandson to Thanksgiving dinner. Unbeknownst to her, her grandson had changed his phone number, and Hinton received the invitation instead.

The tradition has continued every year since, with the pair sharing updates about their friendship on social media.

The upcoming Lifetime movie has been in development in various forms for years. Leslie initially approached Dench about adapting the story in 2018 while working at Netflix, but the project was eventually abandoned following downsizing at the company.

Breaking: How Much Latency Does a Self-Hosted LLM Gateway Add? Langfuse vs LiteLLM vs AcruxCore

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1253 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • It has been revealed that 7 Day Free Trial.
  • A self-hosted LLM gateway sits between your app and the model provider, so every call pays for one extra hop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

It has been revealed that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

A self-hosted LLM gateway sits between your app and the model provider, so every call pays for one extra hop. We measured that cost for three open-source gateways: the Langfuse AI Gateway, the LiteLLM proxy and AcruxCore. Each one ran on the same machine, in front of the same OpenAI model. LiteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to every non-streaming call. AcruxCore added 15 to 24 ms. Langfuse's number could not be told apart from zero.

The bigger lesson was about the measurement itself. Before we controlled for it, one OpenAI network address moved our results by more than any gateway did.

Each number is the median time a gateway added to a direct OpenAI call, with its 95% interval in brackets. A gateway can log each call, and logging takes time, so we ran the test three times with three logging levels.

The direct call took 781 to 831 ms at the median, so even LiteLLM's cost is under 9% of a short call. Read the tables this way:.

The obvious test is to time 100 calls through the gateway, time 100 direct calls, and compare the two medians. That test gives the wrong answer, for two reasons.

The first reason is noise. OpenAI's own response time moved by hundreds of milliseconds between calls in our runs. The direct call's p95 was 1,047 to 1,233 ms against a median near 800 ms. A gateway that adds 20 ms is hidden inside that spread unless the test removes it.

It has been revealed that the second reason is the network path to OpenAI. It does not stay the same between a direct client and a gateway, and that difference can be larger than the gateway itself.

In a recent development, api.openai.com resolves to more than one address. From our network, DNS returned two Cloudflare addresses, and one was much farther away than the other. We measured both with a script that pins one address at a time:.

It has been revealed that on a connection that is already open, both addresses answer in the same time. On a fresh connection, the far address adds about 250 ms, because the TCP and TLS handshakes take that much longer.

Recent findings suggest that A gateway keeps its connection to OpenAI open between calls. It pays the setup once and then stays on whichever address it reached first. A client that opens a new connection for each call pays the setup again on every call. How much it pays depends on which address DNS returns that time.

Node's built-in fetch closes an idle connection after about 4 seconds. So a test client that calls OpenAI every few seconds reconnects on almost every call. In our first, uncontrolled run, the Langfuse gateway came out 43 ms faster than calling OpenAI directly. A gateway cannot be faster than the call it forwards. The direct client paid for new connections, and the gateway did not.

The fix has two parts. First, pin api.openai.com to one address on every path. In Docker, that is an extra_hosts entry on each gateway container:.

Second, let the direct client keep its connection open, as a gateway does. With undici, the HTTP client behind Node's fetch, that is a custom Agent:.

Recent findings suggest that we then listed each container's open connections to confirm that every path used the same address. The edge-check script is in the repository linked at the end, and it takes about a minute to run from your own network.

Sources indicate that this advice also applies outside benchmarks. If your app calls OpenAI directly from Node, keep the connection open between calls. Otherwise some of your calls pay the handshake, and on a far address that costs about 250 ms.

It has been revealed that each test sent 150 rounds after 5 warm-up rounds. One round calls OpenAI directly and through each gateway, once without streaming and once with streaming. The order rotates every round, so no path always goes first or last.

Sources indicate that for each round, the script takes the gateway's time minus the direct call's time in that same round. Calls in one round are made within a few seconds of each other, so a slow moment at OpenAI hits all four paths together and cancels out of the difference. The script then reports the median of the 150 differences.

In a recent development, the interval comes from a bootstrap. The script draws 150 differences at random, with replacement, and takes their median. It repeats that 2,000 times, and the middle 95% of those medians is the interval. This is a shortened version of the script's function:.

An interval that includes zero means the test could not separate the gateway's cost from zero. That is what the Langfuse rows show. It does not prove that the cost is zero.

Every call used OpenAI gpt-6-luna with reasoning_effort: "none", the same short prompt and a cap of 5 output tokens. A short answer keeps the model's own time small, so more of the measured time belongs to the path. Each streamed call measured the time to its first token. Each non-streamed call measured the time to the full response.

All three gateways did real work on every call, which made the comparison fair:.

The three logging levels mapped to these settings:.

Recent findings suggest that the machine was an AMD Ryzen 9 5900X with 62 GB of RAM, running Fedora Linux and Docker 29.9. All three stacks ran on it at once, and the test was run on 10 November 2026.

In a recent development, liteLLM added 61 to 67 ms to the full response, but only 9 to 43 ms to the first streamed token. The first token arrives as soon as the model starts to answer, so time spent before that point highlights up in both numbers. The larger cost without streaming suggests that most of LiteLLM's extra time is spent after the model has answered. We did not profile LiteLLM to confirm this.

Logging level made no clear difference for any gateway. Adding LiteLLM's Langfuse callback did not raise its cost. AcruxCore's median rose from 15 ms with logging off to 24 ms with full logging, but its intervals overlap across all three runs. AcruxCore's median is 16 to 24 ms above Langfuse's, and those intervals overlap too, so this test does not rank the two of them.

In a recent development, if 60 ms per call matters to you, as in a chat app that makes several model calls per user message, LiteLLM's cost is real and repeatable. Langfuse and AcruxCore stayed near or within the noise. If your calls take several seconds, any of the three costs less than OpenAI's own variation from one call to the next.

Before you trust a gateway number, your own or anyone else's, check two things. Was each gateway compared with a direct call in the same round? And did the direct client keep its connection open on the same OpenAI address as the gateway? Without both, the result measures the network path and not the gateway.

The scripts, Compose files and raw results are on GitHub: scripts/comparison/langfuse-gateway-vs-litellm-vs-acruxcore.

Talha Anwar is a senior AI and full-stack engineer and writes about building and running AI systems.

The announcement comes as Taco Bell continues to revive older menu items, including the Quesarito, Flamin’ Hot Grilled Cheese Burrito, and Cheesy Street Chalupas, which have recently returned for limited-time runs.

Sources indicate that however, the latest comeback wasn’t decided by Taco Bell executives. Instead, the manufacturer allowed fans to choose which discontinued item would return as part of its inaugural Live Más Open golf tournament, hosted by comedian Kevin Hart.

Taco Bell has confirmed that the Steakhouse Boss Burrito will return to participating US restaurants for a limited time in 2027, marking its first appearance since 2016.

Originally introduced as the Steakhouse Burrito, the returning item features a warm flour tortilla filled with a choice of grilled, marinated steak or marinated all-white-meat chicken.

The burrito includes twice the amount of meat found in Taco Bell’s Steak Grilled Cheese Burrito, along with warm queso sauce, bacon, seasoned potatoes, and reduced-fat sour cream.

It also features a three-cheese blend consisting of mozzarella, pepper jack, and cheddar.

The decision to bring back the burrito came during Taco Bell’s Live Más Open, which took place at The Ranch at Laguna Beach in California earlier this month.

The nine-hole golf tournament featured celebrities, athletes, and Taco Bell fans competing for the opportunity to revive a discontinued menu item.

Team Pink, consisting of Taco Bell fan Abby Abel, professional skateboarder Sean Malto, influencer Emira D’Spain, and reality television personality Serena Page, secured the victory following a sudden-death putting playoff against Team White.

Taco Bell is making fans win a golf tournament to bring back a discontinued menu item.

Taco Bell quietly tests Fire Piña Hot Dog on exclusive secret menu.

Taco Bell revives Shredded Beef Dipping Taco alongside new beef loaded Nacho Fries.

Their prize included championship jackets, a trophy, and the opportunity to select a former Taco Bell menu item for a nationwide comeback.

The tournament also featured a Taco Bell drive-thru on the golf course, serving exclusive items including the Fire Piña Hot Dog, Baja Caesar Crispy Chicken Crunchwrap, and Fiesta Potato Salad.

The Live Más Open is available to stream on Peacock beginning November 20, with a television broadcast scheduled for November 23 on Golf Channel.

Taco Bell has not announced an exact release date or pricing for the Steakhouse Boss Burrito, although the firm confirmed it will be available nationwide for a limited time in 2027.

The announcement follows several other menu changes from Taco Bell, including the return of the Quesarito and the upcoming Make It Flamin’ Hot customization option, which will allow customers to add Flamin’ Hot Fritos to eligible menu items beginning November 24.

In a recent development, the pages of a site form a graph. Think of it as many nodes connected to each other via edges. Each of the edges are the links between the pages, and the nodes themselves are the pages. Now if you start to visualize this as a graph, you will promptly see that there are multiple ways to traverse this graph and reach a particular endpoint.

A search crawler usually uses one of these pages as a starting point and crawls through all of the pages (especially when pages are not fully covered in a sitemap).

If a page lies very deep from the home page, it means that it's not an crucial page. It's an indication to the search engine that this is not something that you yourself consider important, and the search engine has a lesser incentive to rank this page over pages that are linked better within your site.

Sources indicate that the key metric here is link depth. That is the number of clicks it takes to reach a particular page from your home page.

Recent findings suggest that another key metric is broken links. If you have too many broken links, it indicates to the search engine that your site is outdated and not well maintained, and the search engine will then not want to rank your site.

The way to identify both these problems is the same: to actually walk through your site, do a crawl of your site outside in, and try to figure out what the link depth is and if there are broken links on your website.

Seed the crawl with the home page and all URLs mentioned in the sitemap. Technically, the sitemap is not required if you're doing a crawl, but going from the sitemap will allow us to detect orphaned pages as well.

Fetch the pages and follow redirects as required. Record when you're following a redirect: we do not let fetch follow it silently, we record each hop and add its target to the crawl. Record HTTP errors as they occur.

In a recent development, drop URL fragments and tracking parameters. Keep trailing slashes because sometimes there can be mismatches around expectation of trailing slashes in different URLs of a site.

In order to navigate from the home page, we can use BFS. So we know that the first time we reach a page, that is the page's shortest path.

We can cut off the depth over a certain threshold, say 5, to indicate that pages beyond that are too far or too deep to be reached.

Noindex pages will still be crawled. However, we need to make a record of them being not indexed, to reflect that they will not be present in the search engine.

The desired page depth is as close to the home page as possible. Key pages should be close to the home page. The deeper you go from the home page, it signals to the search engine that the page is less important.

The suggested fix for this is that we link the pages from as close to the home page as possible:.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An old leak claiming Rockstar’s next game would be an LA Noire sequel about the Zodiac Killer is back in the spotlight after GTA 6 players discovered that the same source described the game’s ending correctly.

The claims were shared on GTAForums in 2023 by user Shahanshah, who relayed a post from an anonymous 4chan user that also covered several GTA 6 story details.

Now that GTA 6 is out on PlayStation and Xbox, players on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit have gone back through the post and say its ending details match the final game.

The same source had already been credited with details Rockstar confirmed before launch, including Jason and Lucia’s relationship and the game’s Criminal Profile system.

According to the post, the sequel moves the series from 1940s Los Angeles to San Francisco, with a story built around the unidentified Zodiac Killer.

Industry observers note that “You’re not gonna believe me, but Noire 2. Set in San Fran. Zodiac killer,” the post reads.

It added that the game was “still in the very early stages of development, though, it’ll probably be 2030 when it comes out.”.

The source also claimed Rockstar wants to bring back the facial-scanning tech the original LA Noire was known for, and push it much further than seen previously.

“The higher-ups are talking about doing the face scanning stuff again, but making it insane. They want it to be the best looking game ever made,” the post said.

According to recent reports, the rumor first did the rounds in September 2026, before the GTA 6 details could be checked against the finished game. None of the LA Noire 2 claims have been confirmed.

Rockstar LA Noire sequel leak proven fake amid GTA 6 rumors.

Rockstar reportedly furious by GTA 6 leaks but won’t change Netflix premiere date.

Massive GTA 6 leak gains credibility amid Rockstar’s official reveal.

Rockstar does already have a studio with close ties to the original, which was developed by Team Bondi and published by Rockstar in 2011.

Team Bondi founder Brendan McNamara went on to start Video Games Deluxe, which worked on the 2017 LA Noire re-release before Rockstar bought it and renamed it Rockstar Australia in 2025.

Rockstar hasn’t revealed what Rockstar Australia is working on, and has yet to announce a new LA Noire game.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A North Carolina woman was evicted from her apartment after an AI leasing assistant mistakenly told her she could delay paying nearly $4,000 in overdue rent.

Laura Mack, a resident of Colony Townhome Apartments in Raleigh, received an email on November 8 asking when she could pay her outstanding balance of $3,934.17.

It has been revealed that mack responded that she wanted to pay on November 30 and received written confirmation that the date was acceptable. However, eight days later, she was served with an eviction notice.

When Mack contacted the leasing office, she stated an employee explained that the emails had been sent by Olivia, the apartment complex’s AI assistant, which had mistakenly approved her request.

The complex had introduced Olivia to residents in December 2025, explaining that the assistant could answer questions about rent and maintenance around the clock.

Although previous emails from Olivia had been clearly identified as AI-generated, the November 8 messages were signed by Colony Townhome Apartments and did not disclose that they had been written by a chatbot.

Mack said she believed she was communicating with a member of staff, particularly because the emails referenced a bathroom ceiling leak that had taken almost two weeks to repair.

“I thought it was someone from the office because all my information was in there and it mentioned my bathroom,” she told WRAL.

Despite having the agreement in writing, Mack was evicted on November 19. She subsequently stayed in a hotel while trying to determine her next steps.

83-year-old beats $600k fine after house mistakenly listed for rent while she was in hospital.

According to recent reports, “If you told me till the 30th, I’ll get out by the 30th,” she said. “But give me that. You at least honor that. You have to have somewhere where you’re taking responsibility.”.

North Carolina state Sen. Jim Burgin subsequently commented on the case, calling the situation “ridiculous.”.

“Before someone evicted that lady, they should have reviewed their documents,” he told WRAL in a follow-up to the original story.

A spokesperson for Colony Townhome Apartments told the site that the property’s owners were gathering information about the eviction and expected to provide an revision at a later date.

Sources indicate that running an AI agent on your own GPU sounds simple: point it at Ollama and stop paying per token. I set up OpenClaw, an open-source AI assistant, with a 9B model in Ollama on one RTX 3090 and connected it to Discord. Then I read the Ollama log for every request.

It has been revealed that the agent worked. The numbers were not what I expected, though. A one-line question turned into a prompt of more than 18,000 tokens, the first reply took over a minute, and the small model sometimes guessed instead of using its tools.

This article covers what I measured and what each number means if you plan to run an agent on local hardware.

In a recent development, openClaw ran in Docker and reached Ollama on the host at http://host.docker.internal:11434. Discord was the chat interface, and OpenClaw's web panel showed the sessions and context use.

This article is about the results, not the installation. The full step-by-step setup is in a separate guide to running OpenClaw in Docker with Ollama and Discord. That guide covers the Compose file, the Discord bot and how to keep the ports off your network.

All timings below come from the Ollama log on the test machine. Ollama loaded the model with a 32,768-token context.

My first message in Discord was short: "Which model are you running on, and what is 17 * 23?" The bot answered correctly: it ran on ollama/qwen3.5:9b, and 17 × 23 is 391.

The Ollama log showed what that question cost. The model processed 18,415 prompt tokens and generated 33 tokens.

The extra tokens come from the agent itself. With every request, OpenClaw sends:.

According to recent reports, on the RTX 3090, reading that prompt took 10 seconds at 1,838 tokens per second. A slower GPU, or a CPU, needs much longer to read the same prompt.

It has been revealed that prompt tokens per model call, from the Ollama log. Only the first message had to process the whole prompt.

Industry observers note that openClaw counts tokens with its own estimate, which was higher than the Ollama count. The gateway log estimated the prompt at 24,608 tokens, against a prompt budget of 24,576 tokens for this model. By OpenClaw's own count, the base prompt alone used up the budget before any conversation history.

The web panel demonstrated a similar figure: 68 to 69 percent of the context window was in use for the Discord sessions after only a few messages.

The first message arrived while the model was not loaded in GPU memory. That reply took 1 min 10 s:.

The next requests were much faster:.

Reply times on the test machine. Loading the model took most of the first reply.

Recent findings suggest that the speed-up comes from prompt caching. The system prompt, tool definitions and workspace files at the start of the prompt stay the same between requests. Ollama kept that part cached and processed only the new tokens. The model wrote at 91 to 96 tokens per second in every test.

Ollama's documentation claims models stay in memory for 5 minutes by default before they are unloaded. After that, the next message pays the load time again. You can change this with the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE environment variable on the Ollama server, or with the keep_alive parameter per request. A negative value, such as -1, keeps the model loaded. I did not change this setting in the test.

If you run Ollama in Docker, pass the variable with -e OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 or in the environment: section of your Compose file.

Two things used the GPU besides my chat messages.

A heartbeat. OpenClaw's web panel listed one scheduled automation, heartbeat-main, which runs every 30 minutes. The agent wakes on that schedule, so the model gets called even when nobody chats. With Ollama's 5-minute default, the model is unloaded between heartbeats unless someone chatted recently, so a heartbeat most likely starts with a model load. I did not measure this.

An embedding model. During the first message, OpenClaw also called Ollama's /api/embed endpoint twice to index its memory. It used qwen3-embedding:4b, which was already installed on the Ollama server. I did not set OpenClaw to use that model; it picked it on its own.

The two models took this much GPU memory:.

That is 11.4 GB for the models alone, almost half of the RTX 3090's 24 GB.

The rest of the stack was light:.

What this means for you: initiative GPU memory for the chat model, the embedding model and the context, not the chat model alone. If the GPU also runs other models, the heartbeat can compete with them.

It has been revealed that the first two tests in Discord: a question, then a file written with a tool. The user name is blurred.

The mistakes demonstrated up when the model had to check something:.

Sources indicate that after the restart, the bot claimed it had lost the earlier session. When asked to use its read tool, it read the file correctly.

The fix for the first problem was simple. When I wrote "use your read tool to open homelab-test.md", the model opened the file and listed all three points correctly. Naming the tool made it check instead of guess.

The model listed four files and missed the test file and a folder, because it answered from its prompt.

Based on this test, a local 9B model on one consumer GPU works for:.

If you need better answers, OpenClaw also works with hosted models, but then your prompts leave your machine.

According to recent reports, in this test, qwen3.5:9b used 6.3 GB and the qwen3-embedding:4b memory model used 5.1 GB. Together the two models needed 11.4 GB.

The model had to load into GPU memory first, which took 59 seconds of the 70-second reply. Ollama keeps a model loaded for 5 minutes by default, and the OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE setting changes that.

Every request includes OpenClaw's system prompt, its tool definitions and its workspace files. A one-line question became an 18,415-token prompt in this test.

According to recent reports, yes. A heartbeat automation runs every 30 minutes and calls the model even when nobody sends a message.

Recent findings suggest that it handled questions, arithmetic and file creation correctly in this test. It sometimes answered from its prompt instead of using its tools. When it wrongly remarked its memory was lost, asking it to use its read tool made it check the file and answer correctly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake are being hit with waves of zero-score user reviews on Metacritic, with fans of each game appearing to target the other.
  • The two share more than a fanbase rivalry, as GTA 6 landed a 99 Metascore at launch, tying the original 1998 Ocarina of Time for the highest critic score in the site’s history.
  • While critics have been near-unanimous in their praise, GTA 6’s user score on PlayStation 5 has fallen to 5.0, with thousands of negative ratings arriving within a day of launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake are being hit with waves of zero-score user reviews on Metacritic, with fans of each game appearing to target the other.

The two share more than a fanbase rivalry, as GTA 6 landed a 99 Metascore at launch, tying the original 1998 Ocarina of Time for the highest critic score in the site’s history.

While critics have been near-unanimous in their praise, GTA 6’s user score on PlayStation 5 has fallen to 5.0, with thousands of negative ratings arriving within a day of launch.

That’s in stark contrast to the PlayStation Store, where ratings can only be left by players who own the game, and GTA 6 right now holds a score of 4.84 out of 5.

People like this are so lazy. Metacritic is not the only place that people can rate games. But it IS one of the most accessible (meaning it's susceptible to review bombing).PS5 players can rate the games in the Playstation store, and it's at the moment at 4.84/5. https://t.co/BBo090644U pic.twitter.com/s3X7YnbjGX.

Some of the accounts leaving zero scores on Metacritic have barely rated anything else, with Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time remake the only other game on their profile, scored a perfect 10.

One of those reviews blasted Rockstar for “making us wait 13 years for an 80-100$ (maybe invisible or stolen) code in a box that only runs at 30 FPS,” calling it “a buggy mess at launch.”.

Another took aim at the game’s £100 ($132) digital-only price, adding, “This is the beginning of the end for Sony and Rockstar.”.

The Ocarina of Time remake introduced on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5, and by November 8 held a 9.6 user score, the highest in Metacritic’s history.

Recent findings suggest that that has since dropped to 9.0, with a fresh batch of zero scores aimed squarely at Nintendo fans. “Fan forever GTA 6. Go cry fans of Zelda,” one read.

Others were more direct about why they were leaving them, with one zero-score review simply reading, “Y’all losers review bombing GTA 6.”.

GTA 6 is the joint best-reviewed game of all-time.

Zelda Ocarina of Time remake sells 5.2 million copies in four days to break Switch 2 record.

GTA 6 fans concerned for game following major Rockstar leak.

It isn’t clear which side started it, with GTA 6 fans claiming Nintendo players flooded Rockstar’s game first, and some Zelda fans insisting it was the other way around.

Not every negative GTA 6 review is part of the feud, with some players taking problem with the game’s 30fps cap on consoles, frame rate drops, and open-world bugs.

Others have objected to the game’s optional romance system and claimed GTA 6 has gone “woke,” while some simply called it “the biggest disappointment in gaming history.”.

Unlike the PlayStation Store, Metacritic doesn’t require users to prove they own a game before leaving a rating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kaiji Tang, the English voice of Satoru Gojo in Jujutsu Kaisen, states he recorded dialogue for GTA 6 without realizing he was working on Rockstar’s game.

It has been revealed that tang also voices Sanemi Shinazugawa in the English dub of Demon Slayer. He’s played plenty of video game characters, too, including Ichiban Kasuga, the lead in Yakuza: Like a Dragon.

Tang announced his involvement on November 19, the same day GTA 6 debuted on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. He followed up by explaining that he had no idea which game he’d recorded for, adding, “imagine my shock lol.”.

i had no idea what i recorded was for this gameimagine my shock lol https://t.co/Lc1j0WuS0i.

Sources indicate that one fan brought up the line “sit on daddy’s lap” and asked what Tang thought he was recording. Tang joked, “i dunno demon slayer?”.

It has been revealed that when Tang first revealed he was in the game, he gave fans a clue about where to find him. “if you want to find me, watch cartoons in game,” he wrote in a reply.

Tang has three roles in The Johnsons, one of the cartoons players can watch on TV in GTA 6. He voices Jax, a therapist, and a character listed as “Guy in Parking Lot” in Rockstar’s official credits. The episode and character behind the line quoted in the X thread are still unconfirmed.

It has been revealed that the Johnsons is one of several shows made for GTA 6’s in-game TVs. There’s also Macca & Friends, a Saturday morning-style cartoon on Weazel starring the pink alligator featured in the game’s Collector’s Box.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A streamer’s PS5 began smoking while they were away for a toilet break mid-way through their play through of GTA 6.
  • GTA 6 finally rolled out on November 19, following years of anticipation, with millions of players diving into Rockstar’s latest open-world blockbuster.
  • However, the launch hasn’t been entirely smooth, with PS5 and Xbox players reporting game-breaking crashes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A streamer’s PS5 began smoking while they were away for a toilet break mid-way through their play through of GTA 6.

GTA 6 finally rolled out on November 19, following years of anticipation, with millions of players diving into Rockstar’s latest open-world blockbuster.

However, the launch hasn’t been entirely smooth, with PS5 and Xbox players reporting game-breaking crashes. Some have encountered recurring errors that prevent them from progressing, while others have been unable to get past the opening minutes of the game.

On November 21, Twitch streamer JoJoJosiah took to X to share news that their PS5 had begun smoking during a GTA 6 livestream, apparently leaving the console unusable.

“Was playing GTA VI on stream but had to go poop,” they explained. “Paused it and put on a sensory vid for my chat.”.

However, while they were away, the streamer claimed their “PS5 started just smoking out its a**.” The post was accompanied by a video of the incident.

In the video, JoJoJosiah arrives back at their streaming setup to find the room filled with smoke, while they panic and figure out what to do, before the fire alarm goes off.

Was playing gta VI on stream but had to go poop. Paused it and put on a sensory vid for my chatPS5 started just smoking out its ass and now i need to get a replacement 😀 pic.twitter.com/qSdfcCi4l1.

In a reply to the original tweet, the streamer remarked that they were uninjured as a result of the fire. “I’m fine and everything is good tho,” they wrote.

It’s still unclear what caused the console to malfunction, or whether GTA 6 itself played any role in the reported hardware failure, but the streamer revealed that they now need to purchase a replacement console as a result.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Louisiana coffee shop co-owner claims she refused to serve a TikTok creator who returned to her Baton Rouge cafe after posting two negative reviews.

Industry observers note that victoria Arroyo co-owns Pura Vida Coffee Bar, a cafe near Louisiana State University. TikTok creator Fabian Beaucoudray had criticized the shop’s coffee and food in earlier videos, and Arroyo included clips from those reviews in her response.

In one review she also posted to Snapchat, Beaucoudray mentioned she went back to give the cafe a second chance. She took glitch with paying $3 for what she described as five small pieces of potato alongside a $10 sandwich.

It has been revealed that beaucoudray posted about being refused service on November 19. She had returned to the cafe with a friend, according to a recap from TikTok creator thenameisblossom. Beaucoudray wrote in the caption of her own video that she had “never seen a company take a bad review this serious.”.

Arroyo said she was working the register when she recognized Beaucoudray and decided to turn her away. According to Arroyo, Beaucoudray had left both times without mentioning her complaints to staff. Arroyo said that she left the shop without a chance to address the problems before the videos went up.

Arroyo tagged Beaucoudray in her November 20 response and addressed her directly in the caption. “I am genuinely sorry if you were embarrassed today, that was never my intention,” she wrote.

Arroyo’s response passed one million views, while some commenters defended her decision, and others noted the videos made them want to visit the shop.

In a recent development, another TikTok food reviewer drew a public response after criticizing the coffee at a Phoenix bakery. In Atlanta, Keith Lee went viral after his family was refused service at The Real Milk and Honey.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • In a recent development, picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath.
  • Shopify is the fully managed option.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

In a recent development, weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

In a recent development, picking an ecommerce platform is really a decision about which layers you want to own: the storefront, the catalog and order logic, the payment flow, and the hosting underneath. Every platform below draws that line in a different place. If you have already settled the front-end question with a comparison like SitePoint's Astro vs Next.js guide, the next question is what sits behind it. Prices are from each vendor's pricing page as of November 2026.

Shopify is the fully managed option. Basic costs $29 a month with card rates from 2.9% plus 30 cents, and a 2% fee applies to orders processed through a third-party gateway on that plan. Developers get two routes: Liquid themes, or Hydrogen, Shopify's headless toolkit, where your framework owns routing and rendering and Hydrogen supplies the Storefront API client and cart. Templates exist for React Router on Oxygen and for Next.js on Vercel. Plus starts at $2,300 a month.

Whop is a business platform for taking payments and sending payouts, and it sits under a storefront you have already built rather than replacing it. The Checkout element runs in the browser with no server code and no API key on the page. You pass your own order ID as metadata, Whop copies it onto the payment, and your server fulfills from a signed webhook that follows the Standard Webhooks spec. Domestic cards cost 2.7% plus 30 cents with no monthly fee, buyers see payment methods chosen by their location across 195 countries, and the same balance pays out in over 200 countries, including to affiliates or sellers you onboard. Whop's own guide indicates how to integrate a checkout API into a Next.js storefront end to end. The trade-off is that there is no catalog or shipping engine; you collect address fields at checkout and trigger fulfillment from the webhook.

Sources indicate that wooCommerce is a free plugin on WordPress you host yourself, so you own updates, security, and performance. Its payment gateway, WooPayments, charges US merchants 2.9% plus 30 cents per card transaction, 1.5% more for international cards, 2% for currency conversion, and $25 per dispute. Everything is PHP hooks and filters, which makes it the natural pick for agencies already living in WordPress and the wrong pick for anyone who does not want to run a server.

BigCommerce hosts the back end and lets you bring any front end. Core is $29 a month billed annually, capped at $30,000 in trailing annual sales, and plans auto-upgrade as volume grows. There are no platform fees when you use an embedded payment provider, and a 2% fee on Core if you use another one. Catalyst, its reference storefront, is built on Next.js, React Server Components, and the Storefront GraphQL API, and deploys to Vercel.

In a recent development, medusa is an open-source commerce framework in Node.js and TypeScript, with an MIT-licensed core and a commercial enterprise edition. SitePoint covered it when it was still a young Shopify alternative; it now has over 37,000 GitHub stars. Self-hosting is free. Medusa Cloud starts at $29 a month for development, $99 for launch, and $299 for scale, with no percentage of sales, and the company states you can export your data and self-host at any point.

Industry observers note that saleor is a GraphQL-native, API-only commerce platform written in Python and released under the BSD-3 license. Self-hosting is free. Saleor Cloud starts at $1,599 a month for up to $200,000 in monthly sales, with 0.8% on orders above that, and $3,999 a month at the next tier. It is built for teams with a dedicated engineering function and a large catalog, which is exactly who should pay that price.

Recent findings suggest that own only the storefront, and Shopify or BigCommerce will carry the rest. Own everything, and Medusa or Saleor give you a back end you can read. Already on WordPress, and WooCommerce is the obvious fit. Already have a storefront in Next.js or Astro and only need the money to move, and Whop is the shortest path. Whichever you pick, the checkout is where disputes start, so log what SitePoint's friendly fraud guide for developers recommends from day one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A group of elderly residents at a retirement home in France have been introduced GTA 6, and some are already hoping to get their hands on the game for Christmas.

Rockstar Games’ highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launched on November 19, 2026, more than 13 years after the release of GTA 5.

The open-world crime game has attracted enormous attention worldwide, with fans taking time off work to play it. According to French broadcaster TF1, requests for annual leave in France increased by 8% around the game’s launch. Now, the game has been introduced to the older generations.

On November 20, residents at the Domitys senior living facility in Serris, Seine-et-Marne, were introduced to GTA 6 as part of an organized gaming session.

As reported by ICI Paris Île-de-France, the residents swapped their usual activities for an opportunity to explore the game’s virtual world, with many particularly enjoying its boat-driving sequences.

82-year-old Jacqueline was among the most enthusiastic participants, successfully collecting two packages of cocaine during a mission. “I had never touched a controller before 9am this morning. And by 2:30pm, I was fishing out two packages of drugs,” she joked.

Another resident, 86-year-old Lucienne, was equally impressed by the game’s visuals, describing them as incredible and comparing the experience to watching a real film.

Meanwhile, 75-year-old Yvan admitted that the controls were difficult to master, joking that he was no longer 20 and struggled to keep up with the action.

Staff explained that the residents had found driving and shooting particularly challenging, but enjoyed exploring the environment by boat.

The experience proved popular enough that Lucienne said she intended to ask her children for GTA 6 for Christmas, while Jacqueline suggested installing a console in the communal lounge.

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Industry observers note that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Industry observers note that every SSL certificate comes with a limited lifespan. Following the latest patch from the CA/Browser Forum, the maximum lifetime of a certificate has fallen from 398 days to 200, and it will drop to 100 days in March 2027 and 47 days in 2029. Renewal is no longer an annual chore. It’s an ongoing task that only stays manageable with automation.

So what does this mean if you already look after sites with SSL certificates, and will it bring drastic changes? For many setups, very little will change. For others, one missed renewal can mean an outage. This article explains what’s changing and what to do if you’re in the second group.

Recent findings suggest that today, an SSL certificate is valid for 200 days at most. The limit applies when a certificate is issued, so the ones you already hold keep their original expiration date.

According to recent reports, where you feel it depends on how your certificates renew. Sites on managed hosting platforms or behind a content delivery network (CDN) usually renew automatically already, often every 90 days, so the fresh limit changes little. The pressure lands on setups where someone buys a certificate once a year and installs it by hand. At 47 days, that becomes about 12 renewals a year.

Industry observers note that A certificate is a promise from a certificate authority that a key really belongs to a domain, and that promise gets less reliable the longer it runs. If a private key leaks, or a certificate is issued by mistake, it stays usable until it expires. Cutting the lifetime shrinks that window, so a problem that once lingered for over a year is now fixed in weeks.

Shorter lifetimes also make revocation, the process for canceling a bad certificate, far less critical. Revocation has never worked perfectly, but a certificate that expires within weeks matters much less if a cancellation doesn’t reach every browser.

Another reason is about people. A task done once a year is easy to forget and hard to check from outside. Browser makers have pushed for years to move the industry onto automatic renewal, on the logic that a process that runs every few weeks gets tested constantly. If it breaks, you notice swiftly instead of discovering it on the day the certificate expires.

According to recent reports, for most people, the first effect is simply more work. A certificate that once needed attention every year will soon need it every few weeks. Plus, each renewal is a small chance for something to go wrong. Multiply that by dozens of sites, mail servers, and devices, and the chance of one slipping through grows promptly.

The safety nets are also thinner. If you relied on the renewal emails, nothing is watching your certificates now. Additionally, with a shorter life, there’s less time between this should have renewed and this has expired.

Industry observers note that an expired certificate doesn’t make a site slow or dated. It makes it unreachable for most visitors. Chrome, Firefox, and Safari all show a full-page warning that the connection isn’t private, and most people leave instead of clicking through. If the site uses HSTS, a setting that tells browsers to connect only over secure links, there is often no way to click through at all, and visitors are blocked outright until the certificate is fixed.

According to recent reports, the damage doesn’t stop at the home page. Checkouts, contact forms, and logins that depend on the secure connection fail along with it, often without an error message that points at the real cause. Other systems break, too, because apps and integrations that call your site over a secure link refuse to connect to an expired certificate.

Nothing about your site has to change for any of this to happen. A date passes, and a site that worked on Friday is down on Monday. In a 47-day lifetime, that date comes around about every six weeks.

In a recent development, automatic renewal tools do the heavy lifting well. The failures happen around them:.

Sources indicate that look at the five failures above and you’ll see what they share. Each one happens quietly. The renewal job ran, or looked like it did, and nobody checked what the server was actually serving afterwards. Automation can tell you it tried. It can’t tell you the result reached your visitors.

Sources indicate that what closes that gap is a check that never relies on your server’s own account of events. Site24x7’s SSL/TLS certificate monitoring does exactly that. It reads the certificate installed on your web server from the cloud, the way a visitor’s browser would, and alerts you before it expires, using thresholds you choose. If a renewal fails quietly, you hear about it from the monitor and not from a customer.

For each certificate, it records the issuing authority, the owner, the matter date, the expiration date, and the days remaining, including on servers that host several certificates behind one address. That last number matters more as lifespans shrink. When a certificate lasts 47 days, the days left is the figure that tells you a renewal is overdue, and you can set your warning against it using the quarter-of-the-lifetime rule covered next.

Once a monitor is watching your certificates, the next question is when it should speak up.

Most expiration alerts are set to a fixed number of days: warn at 30 days left and escalate at seven. That works for a certificate that lasts a year and renews with a month to spare. It breaks when the whole certificate lasts for a limited number of days.

Here’s why: a healthy certificate renews with about a third of its life still left. If your alert appears earlier than that, it goes off on certificates that are doing nothing wrong, and soon everyone ignores it. As lifespans shrink, a fixed 30-day alert will start doing exactly that.

Recent findings suggest that the fix is to set the alerts based on lateness, not on how close the expiry date is. Warn when a quarter of the lifetime is left, since a renewal is overdue by then, and escalate when a tenth is left. Because these are shares of the lifetime, they keep working, however short lifespans get.

The next cut lands on March 15, 2027, so a few checks now will save you from scrambling later:.

Shorter lifespans won’t break your site, but a missed renewal will, so fix the quiet failures now while a mistake still costs an afternoon to fix, not a Monday morning outage affecting lots of customers.
